close_reason: Replaced silent if-let-Ok with map_err(server_fail_from_backend)?. Required adding two test hooks to MockBackend: set_get_ancestors_err (failure injection on the trait method) and add_get_objects_node (seed a FileNode-shaped JSON value so get_objects returns a non-empty list, which is the precondition for the fetchParents branch to fire). Regression test get_fetch_parents_propagates_get_ancestors_err exercises the full handler path with both hooks armed. Committed in b7eded9. Gates: fmt/clippy/test/doc green; full workspace test suite green.
description:
src/filenode.rs:70-84: 'if let Ok(ancestors) = backend.get_ancestors(...) { ... } // Non-fatal: if ancestors cannot be fetched, return the list without parent nodes. Clients should handle this.'

The fetchParents argument is the *only* signal the client gets that ancestors were requested; the response shape does not indicate failure to expand. If get_ancestors errors, the client gets back a list that looks like a successful fetchParents=true response but contains only the requested nodes — the same shape it would get if every requested node were at depth 0 (root).

Trigger: any get_ancestors backend error (DB timeout, missing index, etc.). Bad behavior: client believes the nodes are at root level when they may have ancestors. Building 'reconstruct the full path' UX (the spec's stated use case at §3.2.1 lines 511-518) produces wrong paths.

Required: propagate the error via server_fail_from_backend, same as the rest of the handlers in this file (e.g., filenode.rs:147). The 'clients should handle this' rationale in the comment is unactionable: clients have no way to detect this case from the wire response.
title: handle_filenode_get: fetchParents backend error silently dropped, partial result returned
